newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P assigns "pi" ratings to nine Malaysian banks.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns "pi" ratings to nine Malaysian banks.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Tuesday it had assigned public information ("pi") ratings to nine Malaysian banks, ranging from A-pi to BB-pi.
Public information ratings, a new service started by S&P late last year, are based on publically disclosed information and do not rely on S&P receiving access to the rated banks' management.

Public Bank Bhd's A-pi rating was based on its strong market position, good asset quality, satisfactory earnings record, strong funding base, high capital ratios and strong management, S&P said in a statement.
But it added that the bank must prudently manage rapid growth and regional expansion.

Bank Bumiputra Malaysia Bhd's BBB-pi rating was based on the total ownership by the Malaysian govenment and the expectation that the government would continue to provide support should the need arise.
But the bank's level of problem loans remained above the industry average and it still faced many challenges to regain market share, S&P said.

Bank of Commerce Bhd's BBB-pi rating was based on its sound market position, improving earnings and sound capitalisation, but constraints included the uncertainties of erratic balance-sheet growth, residual high non-performing loans and lack of non-bank business diversity, the rating agency said.
Perwira Affin Bank Bhd's BBB-pi rating was based on improving earnings performance, a declining non-performing loan level, adequate capitalisation and solid ownership, it said.
But uncertainties associated with high loan and asset growth, slightly below-average funding structure, limited market share and small absolute capital was reflected in the rating.

Ban Hin Lee Bank Bhd's BB-pi rating reflected its small position in the Malaysian banking industry and the increasing competition it faced. Other factors included the central bank's restrictions on branch network expansion for tier two banks, its overall small capital base and relatively high growth rates.

The BB-pi rating on Hong Leong Bank Bhd was reflected in sensitivities associated with the bank's high growth strategy, limited track record under new ownership since 1994 and risks associated with operating in a rapidly growing, developing market, it said.

S&P said Multi-Purpose Bank Bhd's BB-pi rating was based on its small capital base and typically lower than peer group average capital ratios, small market position, vulnerability to competition from larger competitors and risks associated with operating in a rapidly growing, developing market.

Sime Bank Bhd's BB-pi rating was based on its residual asset quality problems and the uncertainty of its ability to recapture lost market share, S&P said. The bank's underlying profitability had reached that of its peers, although after-tax profitability was lower because of continuing bad debt expenses, it said.

The BB-pi rating of Southern Bank Bhd incorporated the bank's small market share and position in Malaysia, relatively high level of non-performing loans on an international basis and its small size which provided only minimal protection against event risk, the rating agency said.
S&P said the performance of the Malaysian economy would be pivotal to the health of the banking sector over the next few years.
